topic.title: How did Russia get so big?
topic.map_answer: Russia's colour spreading east across the map from the Ural Mountains, fort by fort along Siberia's rivers (Ob, Yenisei, Lena), until it reaches the Pacific coast

title: Russia once ended at the Urals. Then what?
description:
How did Russia end up stretching from Europe to the Pacific?
A few hundred Cossacks, Siberia's rivers and a hunger for fur, on the map, river by river.
Sources: Wikipedia (Nov 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Fur or gold: which do you think built more empires? Comment

lines.text: Russia once ended at the Ural Mountains. So how did it reach the Pacific?
Beyond them lay Siberia, a frozen forest so wide it ran all the way to the far side of Asia.
Then a Cossack chief called Yermak crossed them, rowing and dragging river boats, with just 540 men.
A rich merchant family, the Stroganovs, paid for the trip, and Yermak took the capital of the Khan of Sibir.
But what were they really after? Fur. Sable and fox pelts sold for a fortune in Moscow.
So every village they reached paid a tax in furs, called yasak, and each time the Cossacks built a wooden fort to collect it.
How far could that go? Up the Ob, across to the Yenisei, on to the Lena, dragging the boats from river to river, and every new fort became the start of the next run.
The people already living there, Siberia's native peoples, were made to pay, and many who fought back were crushed.
And just one lifetime after Yermak crossed the Urals, Cossacks stood on the shore of the Pacific.
That race for fur is most of why Russia is now the biggest country on Earth, stretching from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific.
Fur or gold: which built more empires? Tell me below. And it all started with a few boats, rowing east from the place where

Beat 'yermak': 'A Cossack chief called Yermak crossed them first' is false. Novgorod traders worked beyond the Northern Urals and reached the lower Ob from the 12th-13th centuries, and Moscow's 1483 campaign (Kurbsky and Saltykov-Travin) and its 1499 campaign crossed the Urals to the Tobol, Irtysh and Ob a century before Yermak. Drop 'first' (e.g. 'A Cossack chief called Yermak crossed them, ...') or say his crossing began the conquest.

Hook/title 'Russia once ended at the Ural Mountains': because of those earlier trans-Ural tribute campaigns this is a simplification. It is acceptable only if the 'first' claim goes; better wording is 'Russia's lands once stopped at the Urals'. Not a reason to fail on its own.

Confirmed: 540 Cossacks under Yermak, July 1581 (en.wikipedia.org Russian conquest of Siberia, fetched); Qashliq, the Sibir capital, taken Oct 1582; ostrogs built to collect yasak fur tribute (Tyumen 1586, Tobolsk 1587); Ob, Yenisei (1605/1619) and Lena (1623/1632) sequence; Pacific reached 1639 (58 years, so 'one lifetime' holds); atrocities against and resistance by native peoples (article); Stroganov sponsorship (Britannica, Yermak Timofeyevich); fur shown as the main but not the only motive ('most of why'), which matches the verify item. Disclaimer present.
